newsitem.title: BURMA: Rangoon hands drugs fugitive to Thailand.
newsitem.headline: Rangoon hands drugs fugitive to Thailand.

text.p: Burma's ruling military government said on Saturday it had handed over to Thai authorities an accused drug trafficker sought by the United States and Thailand.
A Burmese government statement said Li Yun Chung, alias Pongsak Rojanasakul, was handed over to Thai officials on Saturday. He had fled to Burma after jumping bail in Thailand in March.

Burma's ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council said it regarded total eradication of narcotic drugs as a national task and its decision to hand over Li to Thailand was aimed at boosting the region's fight against drug trafficking.

The Bangkok Post on Saturday quoted Thai official sources as saying that Li, who was awaiting a Thai decision on his extradition to the United States when he jumped bail in Bangkok, had been captured by Burmese officials at the Burmese border town of Techilek.

Li, a close aide of Khun Sa, the once notorious drugs kingpin who operated out of the opium-growing Golden Triangle, has been sought by the United States for his suspected link to 486 kg (1,069 lb) of heroin seized in Hayward, California, in 1991.
He was arrested in Thailand in July 1996 at the request of Washington.

Li's handover to the Thai authorities occurred the same day Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh completed his one-day official visit to Rangoon where he discussed border cooperation and joint narcotics suppression.
